delay.title: Measure the device delay
delay.description: Plays a measuring sound from the output and times how long it takes to reach the input. It shows the delay of the combination of devices selected now: microphone, speaker or headphones, audio interface.
delay.setupCable: Connecting the output to the input with a cable (loopback) measures most accurately
delay.setupSpeaker: Without a cable, put the speaker where the microphone hears it. Put earphones or headphones close to the microphone
delay.setupRoom: While it measures (up to 90 seconds) the room does not hear you. The sound starts quiet and gets louder step by step
delay.needsRoom: It can only be measured while you are in a room (so that it measures the devices the room uses)
delay.helperCannotStart: The person being helped measures this on their own screen (the sound comes out of their speakers)
delay.startFailed: Could not start measuring. Check that you are in a room
delay.none: The devices selected now have not been measured yet
delay.review: The delay is over 100 ms. Look at the buffer size and the device settings again (the driver, exclusive mode, whether Bluetooth is in use)
delay.told: The others in the room are told this number (the number only, no sound). Changing the devices or the buffer size means measuring again

failure.no_sound: The sound did not come back. Check the cable, or the position and volume of the speaker and microphone
failure.unsteady: The values varied widely between plays. Reduce the noise around you and measure again
failure.too_long: The delay is too long to measure (over 0.5 seconds). Look at the device settings again
failure.no_stream: The audio has not started yet. Wait a moment and try again
failure.timed_out: It could not finish in time. Try again

limiter.title: Limiter
limiter.inputHint: Keeps the sound you send from going over 0 dBFS. Adds no delay
limiter.outputHint: Keeps the sound you hear from going over 0 dBFS, even when everyone plays at once. Adds no delay

wasapi.label: WASAPI (Windows Audio Session API) mode
wasapi.about: What is WASAPI (Windows Audio Session API)?
wasapi.aboutText: It's the part of Windows that apps use to play and record sound. jamuru opens any device that isn't an ASIO one through it. In shared mode, Windows processes the sound of every app together at a fixed period (usually 10ms), which adds to the latency. In exclusive mode, jamuru skips that processing and uses the device directly
wasapi.description: How Windows opens a device that isn't an ASIO one. Each mode is marked for the devices you're using

reason.nothing_faster: With this device, no other mode lowers the latency
reason.faster_available: With this device, another mode gives lower latency
reason.shorter_period: Runs at a shorter period than the standard one. Other apps can still play through the same device
reason.same_period: This device's driver doesn't offer a period shorter than the standard one, so the latency stays the same
reason.buffer_longer: The buffer is longer than the standard period, so the latency stays the same. A smaller buffer lowers it
reason.no_low_latency_mode: Not available on this version of Windows
reason.no_exclusive_format: This device has no format it can be opened in exclusively
reason.exclusive_not_allowed: Windows doesn't let apps take this device exclusively. To use this mode, in Control Panel > Sound, open this device's properties and, on the Advanced tab, turn on "Allow applications to take exclusive control of this device"
reason.unknown: Couldn't read what this device supports. Choosing it tries it, and a device it doesn't open is opened in the standard shared mode

wasapi.exclusiveCaution: While in exclusive mode, other apps can't play sound through this device. With Windows' default settings, an app already playing through it goes silent too
wasapi.notApplied: Both the input and the output are ASIO devices, so this mode isn't used

previousHang.title: Last time
previousHang.description: jamuru did not close normally last time - it seems to have been stuck while {{stage}}. Send a small report (nothing about your audio, chat or rooms) so this can be found and fixed?
previousHang.descriptionWithLog: jamuru did not close normally last time - it seems to have been stuck while {{stage}}. Send a small report, together with the current jamuru.log, so this can be found and fixed? The log can include the server address, your audio device names, the room ID, and other participants' identifiers.

privacy.usageDescription: Off by default. When you turn it on, jamuru sends how it runs on your machine to the jamuru server, so that problems on particular machines and connections can be found and fixed.
privacy.usageSent: Sent: app version, OS, CPU and memory, audio device names, IDs and what they support, your settings (a custom server URL only as far as its host and port), totals for each session (length, latency, packet loss, what kind of route the audio took and how long it took to connect), your own IP addresses (on your networks and the public one), the kind of each error, and where a crash happened.
privacy.usageNotSent: Never sent: display name, room history, machine identifier, anything about the other people in the room (their IP addresses included), audio, chat.
privacy.usageDeviceNames: Device names are sent as your system reports them. If a name contains your own name, such as "Taro's AirPods", it is sent too. Check the exact text with "Show what is sent".
privacy.usageIdNote: Turning it on creates a random install ID that ties your reports together. Turning it off discards the ID and anything not yet sent.
privacy.usagePreviewEmpty: Nothing is waiting to be sent yet.
privacy.usagePreviewOff: Off: nothing is collected or sent, and there is no install ID.

diagnostics.description: Diagnose network, audio, and CPU performance to recommend optimal settings.

noIpv6.suggestion: IPv4 will be used instead. This is fine for most connections.

perDestinationNat.message: This router uses a different port for each peer
perDestinationNat.suggestion: Peers behind a router that does the same are hard to reach over IPv4.

upnpOff.message: Opening the router's port automatically is off
upnpOff.suggestion: Turn on "Open a router port automatically" under General in Settings to reach more peers.

upnpNoRouter.message: The router did not answer UPnP
upnpNoRouter.suggestion: Turn UPnP on in the router's settings to reach more peers. Restarting the router sometimes helps.

upnpRefused.suggestion: Turn UPnP on in the router's settings to reach more peers.

upnpDoubleNat.message: Another router sits outside your router
upnpDoubleNat.suggestion: Turn off the router function of the line's device (ONU or home gateway) or set it to bridge mode. If IPv6 works, peers connect over IPv6.

ipv6Unreachable.message: IPv6 has an address but cannot reach out
ipv6Unreachable.suggestion: Check the router's IPv6 settings. IPv4 still works without it.

stunUnanswered.message: Could not check how your line looks from outside
stunUnanswered.suggestion: UDP may not be getting out. Turn off the VPN or security software, or try another network.

microphoneRefused.message: The OS does not let jamuru use the microphone
microphoneRefused.suggestion: Turn on jamuru in System Settings → Privacy & Security → Microphone, then quit jamuru and open it again.

microphoneUndecided.message: The microphone has not been allowed yet
microphoneUndecided.suggestion: The OS asks when you join a room. Choose Allow.

unstableConnection.suggestion: Consider using a wired connection instead of WiFi

wifiConnection.suggestion: Wi-Fi is not recommended for a session: its delay varies and the sound can break up. Use a wired LAN connection.

highJitter.suggestion: Increase buffer size or use a more stable connection

inputEnumerationFailed.message: Failed to get the list of input devices
inputEnumerationFailed.suggestion: Error: {{error}}. Try restarting your audio interface.

outputEnumerationFailed.message: Failed to get the list of output devices
outputEnumerationFailed.suggestion: Error: {{error}}. Try restarting your audio interface.

inputDeviceUnresponsive.message: The input device is not responding
inputDeviceUnresponsive.suggestion: The audio driver did not answer in time, so the input devices could not be read. Reconnect the audio interface, or restart it and the computer's audio service, then run the diagnostics again.

outputDeviceUnresponsive.message: The output device is not responding
outputDeviceUnresponsive.suggestion: The audio driver did not answer in time, so the output devices could not be read. Reconnect the audio interface, or restart it and the computer's audio service, then run the diagnostics again.

noInputDevices.suggestion: Connect a microphone or audio interface

inputNot48kHz.suggestion: Consider using a different audio device

outputNot48kHz.suggestion: Consider using a different audio device

lowBufferUnsupported.message: Current devices may not support ultra-low buffer sizes
lowBufferUnsupported.suggestion: For lowest latency, consider using an ASIO-compatible audio interface (Windows) or a dedicated audio interface

noAsioDevices.suggestion: ASIO provides the lowest latency on Windows. Consider installing ASIO4ALL or using an audio interface with native ASIO support.

insufficientRealtimeHeadroom.message: CPU may not provide enough headroom for real-time processing
insufficientRealtimeHeadroom.suggestion: Close other applications or use a larger buffer size

highCpuUsage.suggestion: Close other applications to free up CPU resources

lowMemory.suggestion: Close other applications to free up memory

smallBufferGlitchRisk.suggestion: Consider using a larger buffer size (64 or 128 samples)
